Bronze is EcoVadis's lowest published medal tier — it signals baseline performance, not comprehensive compliance with every regulation
key-players-institutions.explanation: EcoVadis medals run Bronze through Platinum — Bronze is a real but modest result, useful context rather than a guarantee of full compliance across every ESG dimension a buyer might care about.

timeline-milestones.question: A colleague claims CSRD's reporting requirements have stayed exactly the same since it was adopted in 2022. What should you correct them on?
options: The 2026 Omnibus reform significantly narrowed CSRD's scope and simplified the ESRS by roughly 61% of mandatory datapoints
CSRD has been fully repealed
CSRD was actually adopted in 2015, not 2022
Nothing — they're right, CSRD hasn't changed
timeline-milestones.explanation: The 2026 Omnibus reform is a real, substantial change — the revised ESRS adopted in July 2026 cut mandatory datapoints by roughly 61% and narrowed CSRD's scope. Treating the 2022 text as still fully current is a common but outdated assumption.

timeline-milestones.question: A colleague asks why CSDDD's timeline changed from a staggered rollout to one single date. What happened?
options: The 2026 Omnibus reform replaced the staggered wave rollout with one single application date (26 July 2029) for all in-scope companies
CSDDD never had a staggered rollout to begin with
The change only affects companies outside the EU
The original CSDDD was withdrawn and replaced entirely
timeline-milestones.explanation: This is a direct, concrete effect of the 2026 Omnibus reform — instead of tracking which 'wave' a company fell into, everyone in scope now works toward the same single 2029 deadline.

csrd-esrs.question: Your company's carbon emissions barely move the needle on your financial statements, but they visibly affect air quality in the town where your factory sits. Does ESRS require you to report on them?
options: No — if a topic isn't financially material, ESRS doesn't require disclosure on it
Yes — under double materiality, a topic is reportable if it is material either financially or for its impact on people and the environment, and this clearly qualifies as impact material
Only if a competitor already discloses it
No — ESRS only ever assesses financial materiality; impact materiality was dropped in the Omnibus reform
csrd-esrs.explanation: Double materiality means a topic can require disclosure for either reason on its own — its effect on the company's finances, or the company's effect on people and the planet. Local air-quality impact is a textbook impact-materiality case, independent of whether it shows up on the balance sheet.

csrd-esrs.question: A company has 600 employees and €300 million in annual turnover. Under the post-Omnibus CSRD thresholds, is it in mandatory scope?
options: Yes — any company over 250 employees was always in scope
No — mandatory CSRD scope now requires exceeding both 1,000 employees and €450 million turnover, and this company clears neither threshold
Yes, because it is a large unlisted company
No — only listed companies were ever in CSRD scope
csrd-esrs.explanation: The 2026 Omnibus reform narrowed mandatory CSRD scope to companies exceeding both 1,000 employees and €450 million in turnover. A company below both thresholds has no mandatory CSRD obligation, even though it would have been in scope under the original, much broader 2022 text.

regulatoryMilestones.title: EmpCo Directive becomes applicable
regulatoryMilestones.description: The ban on unsubstantiated generic environmental claims and offset-based carbon-neutral claims starts being enforced across the EU.

regulatoryMilestones.title: Revised ESRS starts applying
regulatoryMilestones.description: Companies begin reporting financial year 2027 under the simplified ESRS (roughly 61% fewer mandatory datapoints) — with transitional early application already possible from FY2026.

regulatoryMilestones.title: EU Taxonomy revised Delegated Act entered into force
regulatoryMilestones.description: A 10% materiality threshold now lets companies skip assessing minor activities, cutting required datapoints by roughly 64% for non-financial companies.

regulatoryMilestones.title: Omnibus I Directive entered into force
regulatoryMilestones.description: The reform that narrowed CSRD's scope and removed CSDDD's EU-wide civil liability regime and mandatory transition-plan obligation officially took effect.

regulatoryMilestones.title: CSDDD applies to all in-scope companies
regulatoryMilestones.description: The single application date replacing the originally staggered rollout — every in-scope company, regardless of size tier, is covered from this date.

regulatoryMilestones.title: CSRD Wave 2 starts applying
regulatoryMilestones.description: Large unlisted companies (over 1,000 employees, over €450m turnover) must start sustainability reporting for financial year 2027 — the first mandatory reports themselves will be filed and published in 2028.

regulatoryMilestones.title: CSDDD transposition deadline
regulatoryMilestones.description: EU member states' deadline to write CSDDD's Omnibus-revised rules into national law — exactly one year before the directive actually starts applying to companies.

regulatoryMilestones.title: EU Forced Labour Regulation applies
regulatoryMilestones.description: Regulation (EU) 2024/3015 becomes directly applicable across all member states, banning any product made with forced labour from being placed on, sold in, or exported from the EU market.
